title: Mist-net capture histories of 80 Yellow Thornbills in restoration plantings and woodland remnants, South-west Slopes, New South Wales, 2015-2017
creator: Belder, Donna J.; Pierson, Jennifer C.; Rudder, Alexander C.; Lindenmayer, David B.
citation: Belder, D. J., Pierson, J. C., Rudder, A. C., & Lindenmayer, D. B. (2020). Survival and home ranges of woodland birds in restoration plantings [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.m0cfxpp2b
abstract: Annual mist-net capture histories of 80 Yellow Thornbills (Acanthiza nana) banded at 21 restoration plantings, woodland remnants and large reference remnants in the South-west Slopes bioregion of New South Wales, Australia, 2015-2017, one of 13 per-species tables from a woodland-bird survival study (CJS and Barker models). Site attributes (planting or remnant, size, shape, fencing, planting age) are unit covariates.
samplingProtocol: Mist netting (two 6 m and four 9 m nets at fixed net sites) over two consecutive days per site each year, about four hours before sunset and four hours after dawn; initial banding July-October 2015, recapture and banding June-August 2016 and 2017; birds banded with metal bands, ten species also colour-banded.
surveyEvidenceNote: Every site was netted in each of the three years with the same net sites (paper, Methods); every listed site has captures in every year (asserted). y = 0 is a banding year in which the bird was not caught.
closureNote: one annual banding session per period (two netting days per site, not deposited separately)
geographicCoverage: 21 woodland sites (12 restoration plantings, 6 remnants, 3 reference remnants) in the South-west Slopes bioregion, New South Wales, Australia (about 35.2-35.9 S, 147.1-147.7 E)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: site coordinates as deposited; IUCN LC, not flagged

notShipped.resightings: Barker-model resightings of colour-banded birds between banding sessions (0 birds of this species resighted alive): ad hoc and area-search sightings with no cell in a CJS table; in resight_recap_R5.csv
notShipped.cjs_file: resight_recap_R5_CJS.csv: the banding columns of resight_recap_R5.csv (rebuilt and asserted identical)
notShipped.colour_combination: the colour-band combination (an identifier; colour_banded carries whether a bird had one)
notShipped.tracking: movementdist_SFW.csv, movementdist_WW.csv, territories.csv: home-range tracking, not encounter histories
notShipped.model_estimates: survival, fidelity and home-range model outputs

notes: Species code YET is fixed by the paper and deposit, not expanded in the deposit: the five most-caught codes, in order, match the paper's five most commonly caught species. Wild-caught birds of unknown age carry all three years (E4.4); condition on first capture for CJS. cluster_id is the site; a bird's site and sex are those of its banding row (10 birds that moved site have a dropped second row; 2 of them have a different sex on it). The deposit has 1,259 birds of 38 codes (paper: 1,261 birds of 38 species); 13 codes ship as tables.
